desc:
A positive integer x is automorphic when its square ends with the digits of x itself. For example 5 is automorphic because 52 = 25 ends with 5, and 76 is automorphic because 762 = 5776 ends with 76. The number 10 is not, because 102 = 100 does not end with 10.

Given n, return every automorphic number from 1 to n inclusive, in increasing order.

n = 30    -> [1, 5, 6, 25]
n = 1000  -> [1, 5, 6, 25, 76, 376, 625]
hints: Testing each number directly is correct but too slow near two billion. Think about what the last k digits of x² must equal when x has k digits.
If x has k digits and is automorphic, then x*x - x is divisible by 10<sup>k</sup>. Find all residues modulo 10<sup>k</sup> that satisfy this, and build the list one digit at a time.
Every solution modulo 10<sup>k+1</sup> reduces to a solution modulo 10<sup>k</sup>, so each level can be extended from the previous one. Keep only the residues with exactly k digits at level k.
editorial: A number x with k digits is automorphic exactly when x<sup>2</sup> ≡ x (mod 10<sup>k</sup>). Let S<sub>k</sub> be the residues r in [0, 10<sup>k</sup>) with r<sup>2</sup> ≡ r (mod 10<sup>k</sup>). Any element of S<sub>k+1</sub> reduces to an element of S<sub>k</sub>, so S<sub>k+1</sub> can be generated by trying the ten possible digits in front of every element of S<sub>k</sub>.

The sets stay tiny: each S<sub>k</sub> has exactly four elements, namely 0, 1 and two more residues that end in 5 and 6 respectively. So only a few dozen candidates are ever examined, however large n is.
At level k keep the residues that have exactly k digits (at least 10<sup>k-1</sup>) and do not exceed n. The answer is their sorted union over all levels.
time: O(log n) levels, four residues each
